newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline outshines heat, ends sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline outshines heat, ends sharply higher.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline prices ended sharply higher Friday after the oil complex shook off earlier profit-taking, but volume was light due to a lack of news. "Gasoline for the first time is performing better after being beaten up so much in the last two weeks," said Tom Bentz, an analyst with ING Derivatives.

October gasoline settled up 1.61 cents to 64.60 cents a gallon. Traders were selling heating oil - which has risen more than 25 percent in the last three months - to buy gasoline, perceived as having bottomed after recent heavy selling, dealers said.

"Heating oil has been strong for so long that finally it reversed," said a trader of the heat-to-gasoline spread action. October heating oil settled up 0.59 cent to 71.49 cents a gallon after falling as low as 69.95 cents on profit-taking which lacked the momentum to take heat lower.
November crude settled 44 cents up at $24.60 a barrel, taking direction from heat and gasoline on a lack of news.

"There was no news, and volume was light," said ING's Bentz. November heating oil gained more than the October contract, up 0.89 cent to 71.07, as traders rolled positions ahead of the October expiry Monday for refined products.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
